t: First Matching Character From Both Ends
o: Find the smallest i with s[i] == s[n-1-i]; return -1 if none. Note that when n is odd, the middle index always matches itself, so an answer always exists for odd lengths (example 2 returns 1 for "abc").
k: Direct two-ended comparison; the first hit scanning i upward is the answer.
Odd-length strings always terminate at the middle index.

a.i: Compare s[i] with s[n-1-i] for i = 0, 1, 2, ... and return the first match.
s: For i from 0 to n-1: if s[i] == s[n-1-i] return i.

w: As easy as it looks; only loop to the midpoint if you want micro-optimization (results are symmetric). Edge cases: length 1 returns 0; even-length strings with no mirrored match return -1.
